messages:
sam: quick nsys run on a failing trace — matmul latency spikes when sequence > 2k, attached nsys. cc @maya @kevin

maya: looked a bit — top hotspot points at cublasLt algo fallback during long-context matmuls. nvprof shows workspace allocation failures -> immediate fallback to algorithm 0.

kevin: that matches what I saw after the batching heuristic change (dynamic_window=1.2). batch composition got more variable, so some ops end up requesting larger workspace from cublasLt.

jin: perfetto timeline: kernel bursts line up with kv-cache recompute + several small kernels getting serialized. also saw slab fragmentation markers in our allocator trace.

perf-bot: regression alert: matmul tail latency P95 +18% vs baseline (2026-02-14 rollout). trace_id=abc123.

maya: repro command I used (nsys):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn -o /tmp/run1 --sample=none \
  python -m bench.matmul --batch 8 --seq-len 4096 --warmup 10 --iter 50
```

sam: ran that script locally — consistent pattern: cublasLt tries algos that require ~200-300MB workspace, alloc fails due to fragmentation and we fall back to algo 0 which is slower. GPU free memory shows lots free but allocator can't satisfy aligned slab.

kevin: hypothesis: cublasLt selects algos based on tiling that need contiguous workspace. our workspace provider gives many small free chunks (KV cache preallocs), so large aligned allocation fails even when total free > request. Instead of immediate algo fallback we should probe smaller workspace sizes for the same algo.

jin: batching heuristic also contributes: when sequences are grouped into a larger virtual batch, m/k/n dimensions change so preferred algo changes and workspace balloons. We could enforce a per-algo workspace cap in the batching planner.

maya: patch sketch: 1) implement 'decreasing-workspace probe' for cublasLt candidates (try 256MB -> 128MB -> 64MB before giving up), 2) cache probe results per (shape, dtype, device) to avoid repeated probes, 3) expose slab fragmentation metric to console for alerting.

alex: caching is good but needs eviction TTL + eviction on memory pressure signals, and careful handling for multi-tenant dedicated pools.

sam: :thumbsup: I'll prototype probe-decrease logic this week. plan to canary on a small fraction of traffic. who wants to pair on perfetto parsing?

kevin: I'll pull the perfetto timeline and help with validation. ping me when you have a proto. @maya can you open an issue with traces and nvprof/nsys outputs?

maya: done — INF-1293 contains nsys + perfetto + nvprof logs and a short reproducer. link: https://redwood.internal/INF-1293 :white_check_mark:
